title: SynthID Bio: watermarking for proteins and synthetic structures
summary: Methods insert a detectable signal into protein sequences and predicted structures. For binders designed against three targets (VEGF-A, SARS-CoV-2 RBD, and PD-L1), watermarked designs matched the others in success rate and affinity. This is a proof of concept that needs to be made more robust against tampering.

evidence.tested: Wet-lab tests on three targets (VEGF-A, SARS-CoV-2 RBD, PD-L1), with Adaptyv Bio helping, showed watermarked designs matched unwatermarked ones in hit rate, affinity and diversity; the phage was tested only in bacterial cultures.
evidence.unknown: The watermark must become more robust against deliberate tampering, the bacteriophage work is early-stage, and the post says no single biosecurity measure is a silver bullet.
evidence.ai_role: SynthID Bio guided amino acid choice in a ProteinMPNN variant, adjusted predicted atomic coordinates, fine-tuned part of AlphaFold 3, and was integrated into Evo 2 to watermark a designed phage genome.
